Mohd Sameer Alias Tyagi --Applicant
 Versus
State of Uttarakhand --Respondent
Hon'ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J.
Ms. Diksha Pathak, learned counsel holding
the brief of Ms. Sheetal Selwal, learned counsel for
the applicant.
2. Mr. B.C. Joshi, learned AGA, for the State of
Uttarakhand.
3. The applicant, herein, namely, Mohd.
Sameer @ Tyagi S/o Late Mohd. Ashfak, moved
this bail application under Section 483 of BNSS,
2023 for seeking bail in connection with FIR dated
12.02.2025 bearing FIR No.0034 of 2025, Police
Station Lalkuan, District Nainital, wherein, he is
implicated and chargesheeted for the offences
punishable under Sections 8/22/29 of the NDPS
Act.
4. It is submitted by the learned counsel for the
applicant that the applicant is innocent and has
been falsely implicated, which is evident from the
fact that at the time of the search and seizure,
firstly the mandatory provisions of the NDPS Act,
has not been complied with and furthermore
though the inventory was prepared but it was not
certified by the Magistrate in the manner as
provided under the Rules of 2022, therefore there
is no substantial compliance of Section 52-A of the
NDPS Act, and as such, there are reasonable
ground that the applicant is not guilty of the
offences, as alleged. So far as the antecedent part is
concerned, she submits that there is only one case
of 2022, wherein, the applicant is already bailed
out and after 2022 he was not involved in any
crime, except the present one in which the

recovery as shown appears to be doubtful. She also
submits that in the present case the applicant is
languishing in jail since 12.02.2025 and there is no
substantial progress in the trial since out of 14
prosecution witnesses up till date only 5
prosecution witnesses has been examined. Lastly
she submits that the applicant already suffered
incarceration of more than one year six months,
and on this account also the stringent condition as
stipulated under Section 37 of the NDPS Act, may
be dispensed with.
5. On the other side, learned AGA have not
disputed that there is no substantial progress in
the trial since out of 14 prosecution witnesses up
till date only 5 prosecution witnesses have been
examined. With regard to the inventory, he
submits that the submissions as advanced by
learned counsel for the applicant is completely the
subject matter of trial. With regard to the criminal
antecedent, he submits that the applicant has
criminal antecedent of 2022, in which, he is already
bailed out.
6. In view of the submissions and discussions
as above this Court primarily is of the view that
the twin condition as stipulated under Section 37
of the NDPS Act are fulfilled, and in addition to
this the applicant already suffered incarceration of
more than one year and six months, therefore, this
Court is of the view that the applicant deserves for
bail.
7. Accordingly without expressing any opinion
on the merits of the case, the instant bail
application is allowed.
8. Let the applicant - "Mohd. Sameer @ Tyagi",
be released on bail, on his executing a personal
bond and furnishing two reliable sureties, each of
the like amount to the satisfaction of the Court
concerned subject to the following conditions:-
"(i) The applicant after being released on
bail shall join the Trial Court proceeding on
each and every date without seeking any

unnecessary adjournment.
(ii) The applicant shall not indulge in any
such activity in future."
 (Rakesh Thapliyal, J.)
